description: Machine-readable ground truth for the MQTT teaching capture. A Mosquitto broker (10.10.20.10:1883) serves a small plant in cleartext. An HMI (10.10.20.30, client hmi-scada-01, user hmi_operator) subscribes to plant/+/telemetry; a field sensor (10.10.20.7, client field-sensor-07, user sensor_svc) connects with a Last Will and publishes tank readings the broker fans out. A rogue host at 10.10.20.66 (client mqtt-explorer-x) then connects anonymously, subscribes to '#', receives the leaked telemetry, and publishes a command to plant/tank1/command. Frame count is asserted by build/verify_all.py.

malicious_frame_detail.meaning: Anonymous CONNECT (no username). The broker accepts it (CONNACK rc=0, frame 40), so the client is authenticated as an anonymous session.
Wildcard '#' subscription: the rogue client asks for every topic on the broker and receives all telemetry the broker relays (e.g. the leaked fan-out at frame 50). No ACL prevents it.
Unauthorized PUBLISH to a command topic. With no write authorization, any connected client can command an actuator. If a controller trusts this topic, the attacker drives the process.

identity_note: No link-layer or address forgery is used in this capture (MQTT has no data-link address to spoof). The attacker abuses the broker's acceptance of anonymous connections (frame 38) and the absence of publish/subscribe authorization. This is an authentication-then-authorization failure, not spoofing — contrast with the DNP3 capture's forged dnp3.src.

techniques.name: Unauthorized Command Message
techniques.note: Unauthorized PUBLISH of a START command to plant/tank1/command with no write ACL.

additional_observations.note: No single ATT&CK-for-ICS technique is an exact fit for MQTT wildcard eavesdropping; it maps most cleanly to CWE-862 Missing Authorization. Broadly analogous to Network Sniffing (T0842) but performed at the application layer via a legitimate protocol feature.

cwe: CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function
CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
ttp.auth_classification: The broker DID authenticate the rogue client (anonymous CONNECT accepted, CONNACK rc=0); the injection is therefore an authorization failure, not a lack of authentication.

sensor.role: tank sensor, publishes plant/tank1/telemetry with a Last Will

benign_frames_summary.description: Frames 4-10 are the HMI's authenticated CONNECT/CONNACK and its plant/+/telemetry SUBSCRIBE/SUBACK. Frames 15-33 are the sensor's authenticated CONNECT, its plant/tank1/telemetry PUBLISHes (func 3), broker fan-out to the HMI, PUBACKs, and a PINGREQ/PINGRESP. Frames 46/48 are further legitimate sensor telemetry and fan-out. Attacker-induced frames: 40 (CONNACK to rogue), 44 (SUBACK to rogue '#'), 50 (broker leaks telemetry to the rogue subscriber), 54 (rogue DISCONNECT).
benign_frames_summary.note: Credentials travel in cleartext on 1883 (frames 4, 15) — usernames hmi_operator and sensor_svc are readable on the wire. Payloads are JSON tank readings, e.g. {"level_pct":72.4,"temp_c":21.6,"flow_lpm":11.8}.
